I updated the doc based on discussions there and in the proof of concept. Specifically:

- Constructor returns a value rather than a pointer (pointer can still be used in fields to express optionality)
- Constructor returns an error when called with empty path
- Method calls on a root with an empty path panic
- Library is deliberately unstable
- Removed `Todo` method suffix markers

Ready for further comments, if any.

I'm also open to suggestions regarding the choice of the root for the initial stage of the migration.

It might be easiest to start the migration in Podman, where we can change just Podman, then move up the stack to Buildah, and then progressively work towards storage? It seems like doing the libraries first would potentially cause cascading changes in all our repos and could be ugly

c/storage and especially c/image have fairly strict API stability promises, so we should probably keep existing APIs there , and only introduce parallel ones that use the new library.

But the strict API stability promises are also a good reason to start with Podman-internal conversions, and gather more experience to hopefully arrive at a stable and proven API by the time container-libs adopt this.

> we should probably keep existing APIs there , and only introduce parallel ones that use the new library.

(… and in that way, we might avoid cascading changes and need for immediate caller updates.)
